original_question: Construct explicit presentations of a virtual biquandle that uses the given linear non-commutative representation at classical crossings together with a genuinely informative algebraic structure at virtual crossings.
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies that the problem is about a virtual biquandle, that the classical-crossing part should use a linear biquandle representation, that noncommutativity is relevant, and that the missing ingredient is a nontrivial algebraic structure at virtual crossings rather than simply reusing the ordinary biquandle setup.
missing_details: The paper’s official target is specifically the problem labeled "8. Virtual biquandle" in Section 8.1, so the refined question should stay anchored to that exact problem and not drift into neighboring problems such as faithful virtual-braid actions or the algebra [B,(A−1)(A,B)] = 0.
The paper asks for presentations of the virtual biquandle, not merely for one ad hoc construction.

To make "linear" stand-alone, one should import the paper’s Section 6.1 definition: the labels form an R-module over an associative ring with identity, and the classical switch is given by a 2×2 matrix S = [[A,B],[C,D]] with entries in R.

The classical-crossing structure should still satisfy the biquandle framework from Section 6.1: invertibility of the switch, right invertibility of the induced operations, the set-theoretic Yang–Baxter property, and the biquandle condition.

The draft sounds as if one fixed a specific noncommutative linear representation, but the official problem is broader: it asks for a virtual biquandle with a linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings, not necessarily only the specific quaternionic example.
If one wants to mention the motivating noncommutative model from the paper, it should be identified only as nearby context: the quaternionic linear biquandle with i, j quaternionic and t central.

The phrase "interesting structure at virtual crossings" is intentionally qualitative in the paper; it should be preserved as a requirement for nontrivial additional virtual-crossing data, rather than replaced by a new formal criterion not stated in the paper.

The paper’s nearby context indicates that ordinary biquandle labeling conditions are imposed at classical crossings; the open problem asks for an enriched structure that also assigns meaningful algebraic data at virtual crossings.
refined_question: Construct explicit presentations of virtual biquandles for virtual knots and links in which the classical-crossing data is given by a linear biquandle in the sense of the paper—namely, labels lie in an R-module over an associative ring with identity, possibly noncommutative, and the classical switch has the form S = [[A,B],[C,D]] satisfying the biquandle axioms—while the virtual crossings carry additional nontrivial algebraic structure, so that one obtains a genuine virtual biquandle rather than an ordinary biquandle determined only by the classical crossings.
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because Section 8.1, Problem 8 states almost exactly what your draft says. To make it stand-alone while staying paper-faithful, the rewrite imports only the nearby structural context actually supplied in the paper: Section 6.1 gives the switch-map formulation of biracks/biquandles and the paper’s definition of a linear biquandle over an associative unital ring, while the discussion just before Section 6 gives the motivating quaternionic noncommutative linear example. I did not broaden the question to Problem 9 (faithfulness on virtual braids), Problem 10 (the algebra with relation [B,(A−1)(A,B)] = 0), or later virtual-quandle-homology questions, because those are distinct items in the problem list.
